 Judgment

Though this appeal is listed for Admission, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties,
the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. The claimants are in appeal not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under the judgment and award, dated 04.07.2019, passed in M.V.C. No.189/2017 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and II Additional District Judge, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal'), and praying for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel Sri. Ashok A.Naik for the appellants-claimants, and the learned counsel, Sri S.K.Kayakamath for respondent No.2-insurance company.
Though respondent No.1 is served with the notice, he has remained unrepresented.
Perused the appeal papers as well as the records of the Tribunal.

4. The claimants, who are the parents and an unmarried sister of the deceased Mohammed Sohail Zakirhussain Dambal, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the accidental death of Mohammed Sohail Zakirhussain Dambal that took place on 22.02.2016 involving Innova Car bearing registration No.GA-04/C-8228.
It was stated that the deceased was aged 18 years as on the date of the accident, and was earning more than Rs.15,000/- per month by doing coolie work.
5. On issuance of notice, respondents appeared through their counsel and filed their written statements.
Respondent No.2-insurance company in its written statement denied the averments made in the claim petition.
The insurer contended that the accident occurred solely due to negligence of the deceased himself.
The insurer also contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
Thus, the insurer prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. The Tribunal, on the basis of the pleadings of the parties, framed issues.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, got examined the mother of the deceased as P.W.1, and got marked as Exs.P1 to P.10 in the evidence.
The insurer examined one M.Karthik as R.W.1 and got marked two documents as Exs.R.1 and R.2.

The Tribunal, based on material on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.9,54,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, under the following heads:
1

Towards Loss of Dependency Rs. 8,64,000/- 2 Funeral expenses & obsequies Rs.
10,000/- 3 Transportation of dead body Rs. 5,000/- 4 Loss of love and affection Rs.
75,000/-
Sri. Zakeer
Hussain

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/ per month, adopted multiplier '18', and deducted 50% of the income towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The Tribunal apportioned contributory negligence to an extent of 20% on the deceased.

The Tribunal having found that the driver of the offending car was not holding a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident, saddled the liability to pay compensation on the owner of the offending car and dismissed the claim petition as against the respondent No.2-insurance company.

7. Learned counsel, Sri Ashok A.Naik for the appellants-claimants would submit that the Tribunal committed an error in saddling 20% of contributory negligence on the deceased since the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the offending car.

He contended that the deceased was walking on the left side of the road and while he was crossing the road, the driver of the offending car, without noticing him, in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the deceased which resulted in the death of the deceased on the spot.
Therefore, he prays for setting aside the finding of the Tribunal apportioning contributory negligence on the deceased.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant-claimants would submit that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month and he prays for assessment of the income on higher side.

Further the learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal failed to award 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects to which the claimants would be entitled in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others 1.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would also submit that the claimants would be entitled for loss of consortium at Rs.40,000/- each in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others 2.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the learned counsel for the appellants AIR 2017 SC 5157 2018 ACJ 2782 prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation.

9. Per contra, Sri. S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company would justify the finding of the Tribunal on the contributory negligence and he submits that the Tribunal ought to have saddled contributory negligence on the deceased on the higher side.
Learned counsel would also submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just compensation which needs no interference.
Learned counsel would, further, submit that the claimants would not be entitled for interest on the compensation towards future prospects.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers and the records of the Tribunal, the following points would arise for consideration:
i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in saddling 20% of the contributory negligence on the deceased?
ii) Whether the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?

entities.text: Zakeer Hussain S/O Mohamemd ... vs Imran Khan J Pathan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to the above points would be in the affirmative for the following reasons.

a) The accident that took place on 22.02.2016 involving Innova Car bearing registration No.GA-04/C-8228 and the resultant death of Mohammed Suhail Zakirhussain Dambal is not in dispute in this appeal.
The claimants are before this Court praying for enhancement of the compensation.
b) It is the submission of the claimants that the Tribunal committed an error in saddling 20% of contributory negligence on the deceased.
The accident has taken place on the National Highway.

On a National Highway, the pedestrians are not expected to cross the road at all places of the National Highway; they - 10 - are supposed to cross the National Highway only where Zebra Crossing is provided for or at a place reserved for crossing.
On perusal of the records, it is seen that the deceased was crossing the National Highway at a place where Zebra Crossing was not provided for and contributed to the cause of the accident.

On perusal of the records and the reasons assigned by the Tribunal, we are of the view that the finding of the Tribunal with regard to contributory negligence would not require any interference by this Court.
Therefore, the Tribunal is right in saddling 20% contributory negligence on the deceased.
c) The income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.8,000/- per month is on the lower side.

Taking note of the fact that the accident is of the year 2016 and considering the Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority while settling the accidental claims, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the notional income at Rs.8,750/- per month.
Thus, we are of the - 11 - view that income of the deceased could be assessed at Rs.8,750/- per month.
d) The Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards 'future prospects'.

In terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), if the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary and was aged upto 40 years, the claimant/s would be entitled for addition of 40% of the assessed income toward future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was aged 18 years and as such, the claimants are entitled for addition of 40% of the assessed income towards compensation on the head of 'future prospects'.

e) The deceased being a bachelor and aged 18 years, the Tribunal is right in making the deduction of 50% towards personal expenses of the deceased, and in adopting the appropriate multiplier '18'.

5

f) The monthly income of deceased having been assessed at Rs.8,750/- per month, on adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects, deducting 50% towards personal expenses of the deceased and applying multiplier '18', the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.13,23,000/-
[Rs.8,750 + Rs.3,500(40% of Rs.8,750/-) = Rs.12,250/- less Rs.6,125 (50% of Rs.12,250/-) =
Rs.6,125/- x 12 x 18 ] on the head of loss of dependency.

g) The Tribunal committed an error in granting Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of love and affection'
Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.5,000/- towards transportation of dead body.

The awarding of compensation under the conventional heads will have to be in tune with decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and hence, claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the heads of 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex - 13 - Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra), appellants No.1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased, are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards filial consortium.

h) It is the contention of the learned counsel for respondent No.2-insurance company that the claimants would not be entitled for interest on the amount of compensation awarded towards 'future prospects'.
The said contention cannot be appreciated in the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra).

The settled legal position with regard to awarding of compensation towards future prospects is that if the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, the claimant would be entitled for an addition of 40% of the established income where the deceased was below the age of 40 years; 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has not denied interest on the - 14 - compensation towards 'future prospects.
Therefore, the contention of the insurer cannot be appreciated.

12. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation on the following heads:
1 Towards Loss of Dependency Rs. 13,23,000/- 2 Towards loss of filial Rs. 80,000/-
consortium 3 Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000/- 4 Towards funeral expenses Rs.
15,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 14,33,000/-
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total Sri.Zakeer Hussain S/O Mohamemd ... vs Imran Khan J Pathan on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185926885/
6 compensation of Rs.14,33,000 /- as against Rs.9,54,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
13.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has committed an error in awarding interest on the compensation at the rate of 9%
per annum.
Normally, this Court would award interest on the compensation at rate of 6% per annum taking into consideration the present interest on Bank deposits.
The compensation reassessed by this Court shall carry interest - 15 - at the rate of 6% from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit.

14. The Tribunal, having found that the driver of the offending car was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident, while fastening the liability to pay the compensation on the owner of the offending vehicle, has dismissed the claim petition as against the respondent No.2-insurance company.

However, in terms of the Full Bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur by its Divisional Manager Vs. Yallavva and Another 3, in a accidental claim for compensation, where the driver/rider of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident, it is a case of "Pay and Recover", i.e., the insurance company shall pay the compensation to the claimants, at the first instance, with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant ILR 2020 KAR 2239 - 16 - case also, in terms of the aforesaid decision of the Full Bench of this Court, it is for the insurance company to satisfy the claim at the first instance and thereafter it would be at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending car i.e., the first respondent herein.

15. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The above appeal is allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation Rs.14,33,000 /- as against Rs.9,54,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

7
c) The modified compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

d) The respondent No.2-Insurance Company shall deposit 80% of the compensation now reassessed i.e., 80% of Rs.14,33,000/-,
- 17 - along with interest, before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
The respondent No.2-insurance company is at liberty to recover the compensation paid by it from the owner of the offending car i.e., the first respondent herein in an appropriate proceedings.
e) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
No order as to costs.
